title: Fractions, decimals and percentages
intro: Three ways to write the same amount: {1/2}, 0.5 and 50%. Practise switching between them, adding fractions and finding percentages of amounts.
description: Free KS3 Maths fractions, decimals and percentages questions with answers: equivalent fractions, converting, adding fractions and percentages of amounts, with instant marking and worked answers for Year 7, 8 and 9.

questions.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
questions.hint: Count all the equal parts first. That is the bottom number.
questions.explain: The circle is cut into 8 equal parts and 3 are shaded, so {3/8} is shaded.

questions.q: What fraction is the arrow pointing to?
questions.hint: How many equal steps are there between 0 and 1? How many steps along is the arrow?
questions.explain: The line from 0 to 1 is cut into 5 equal steps, and the arrow is 3 steps along. So it points to {3/5}.

questions.q: Both bars are the same length. Which fraction is bigger?
questions.hint: Compare how far the shading reaches along each bar.
questions.explain: The shading for {2/3} reaches further. You can check with a common denominator: {2/3} = {10/15} and {3/5} = {9/15}, so {2/3} is bigger.

questions.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Sam eats 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza is left?
questions.hint: How many slices are left? How many slices were there to start with?
questions.explain: 8 − 3 = 5 slices are left out of 8, so {5/8} of the pizza is left.

questions.q: Which fraction is bigger than {1/2}?
questions.hint: For each fraction, work out half of the bottom number. Is the top number more than that?
questions.explain: Half of 7 is 3.5, and 4 is more than 3.5, so {4/7} is bigger than {1/2}. In the others the top is less than half the bottom: 3 < 4, 2 < 2.5 and 5 < 6.

questions.q: Which fraction is the same as {1/2}?
questions.hint: In a half, the top number is half of the bottom number.
questions.explain: 3 is half of 6, so {3/6} = {1/2}. You get it by multiplying the top and the bottom of {1/2} by 3.

questions.q: Write {6/8} in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Find a number that divides both 6 and 8 exactly.
questions.explain: Divide the top and the bottom by 2: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. So {6/8} = {3/4}.

questions.q: {2/5} is the same as how many twentieths? Type the missing top number: {2/5} = ?/20
questions.hint: What do you multiply 5 by to get 20? Do the same to the top.
questions.explain: 5 × 4 = 20, so multiply the top by 4 too: 2 × 4 = 8. {2/5} = {8/20}.

questions.q: Write {18/24} in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Try the biggest number that divides both 18 and 24. If you are not sure, divide by 2 and then by 3.
questions.explain: The biggest number that divides both 18 and 24 is 6: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4. So {18/24} = {3/4}.

questions.q: Write {10/15} in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Find a number that divides both 10 and 15 exactly.
questions.explain: Divide the top and the bottom by 5: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 and 15 ÷ 5 = 3. So {10/15} = {2/3}.

questions.q: Which mixed number is the same as {11/4}?
questions.hint: How many whole 4s go into 11? How many quarters are left over?
questions.explain: 11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3. That is 2 wholes ({8/4}) and 3 quarters left over, so {11/4} = 2{3/4}.

questions.q: What percentage of the grid is coloured?
questions.hint: There are 100 squares. Per cent means "out of 100".
questions.explain: 25 of the 100 squares are coloured. Per cent means "out of 100", so that is 25%.

questions.q: Which decimal is the same as {3/4}?
questions.hint: {3/4} is three quarters. How much is one quarter of 1 as a decimal?
questions.explain: One quarter is 0.25, so three quarters is 3 × 0.25 = 0.75. You can also write {3/4} = {75/100} = 0.75.

questions.q: Write 0.4 as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.hint: 0.4 means 4 tenths. Write that as a fraction, then simplify.
questions.explain: 0.4 is 4 tenths, so 0.4 = {4/10}. Divide the top and the bottom by 2 to get {2/5}.

questions.q: Write {3/5} as a percentage.
questions.hint: Make the bottom number 100. What do you multiply 5 by to get 100?

questions.q: Which list goes from smallest to largest?
questions.hint: Change them all to decimals: 35% = 0.35, and {1/3} = 0.333…
questions.explain: As decimals: 0.3 = 0.300, {1/3} = 0.333… and 35% = 0.350. So the order from smallest is 0.3, {1/3}, 35%.

questions.q: Write 45% as a decimal.
questions.hint: Per cent means "out of 100". Divide by 100.

questions.q: Write {7/20} as a decimal.
questions.hint: Make an equivalent fraction with 100 on the bottom.

questions.q: Write {3/8} as a decimal.
questions.hint: Start with {1/8}. It is half of {1/4}, and {1/4} = 0.25.
The bottom numbers are the same, so add the top numbers only.
questions.explain: Both are sevenths, so add the tops: 2 + 3 = 5. The answer is {5/7}. The bottom number stays 7.

questions.hint: Change {1/2} into quarters first.
Find a number that both 3 and 4 go into, and change both fractions to have it on the bottom.
To multiply fractions, multiply the tops together and the bottoms together.
questions.explain: Tops: 3 × 2 = 6. Bottoms: 4 × 5 = 20. So the answer is {6/20}, which simplifies to {3/10}.

questions.q: Work out {1/3} + {1/6}. Give your answer in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Change {1/3} into sixths first.

questions.q: Work out 1{1/2} + 2{2/3}. Give your answer as a mixed number, for example 3 1/5.
questions.hint: Add the whole numbers first. Then add {1/2} and {2/3} using sixths.

questions.q: Find 50% of 36.
questions.hint: 50% is the same as a half.
questions.explain: 50% is a half, and half of 36 is 36 ÷ 2 = 18.

questions.q: Find {3/4} of 20.
questions.hint: First find {1/4} of 20 by dividing by 4.

questions.q: Find 10% of £45. Type the answer in pounds.
questions.hint: To find 10%, divide by 10.

questions.q: Find 25% of 80 kg.
questions.hint: 25% is the same as a quarter.

questions.q: A jacket costs £60. In a sale, the price goes down by 15%. What is the sale price in pounds?
questions.hint: Find 10% and 5% of £60, add them to get 15%, then take that away from £60.
questions.explain: 10% of £60 is £6, and 5% is half of that, £3. So 15% is £6 + £3 = £9. The sale price is £60 − £9 = £51.

questions.q: A class has 12 girls and 18 boys. What percentage of the class are girls?
questions.hint: First find how many children there are altogether. Then write the girls as a fraction of that.
questions.explain: There are 12 + 18 = 30 children. Girls are {12/30} = {4/10} of the class, and {4/10} = {40/100} = 40%.

questions.q: There are 30 children in a class. {1/5} of them walk to school. How many children walk to school?
questions.hint: To find {1/5} of something, divide it by 5.
questions.explain: 30 ÷ 5 = 6, so 6 children walk to school.

questions.q: Mia has £8 pocket money. She spends 75% of it on a new game. How much does the game cost? Type the answer in pounds.
questions.hint: 75% is the same as {3/4}. Find {1/4} first.

questions.q: A puppy weighs 4 kg. Over two months its weight goes up by 35%. How much does it weigh now, in kilograms?
questions.hint: Find 35% of 4 kg (try 10% and 5% first), then add it on.
questions.explain: 10% of 4 kg is 0.4 kg, so 30% is 1.2 kg. 5% is half of 10%, 0.2 kg. So 35% is 1.2 + 0.2 = 1.4 kg. The new weight is 4 + 1.4 = 5.4 kg.
